pages.text:
Nila and Tara were making a lantern for the evening fair.

It had orange paper sides, a green handle, and tiny stars cut around the top. When a light was placed inside, stars would shine on the wall.

“Our lantern will be the best!” said Nila.

Tara smiled. “Our lantern.”

They placed it on the classroom table to dry.

Near the door, a little goat from the school garden peeped inside. It had a red ribbon around its neck and a very serious face.

“Shoo, Moti!” laughed the gardener. “Paper is not lunch!”

The goat sneezed.

The children laughed.

After lunch, Nila ran back to see the lantern.

It was broken.

One side was crushed. The handle was bent. One star was torn.

Tara stood near the table, looking worried.

“What happened?” Nila asked.

Tara looked down. “It fell.”

“How?”

“I don’t know,” Tara said.

Nila felt angry. “You were here!”

Tara picked up her bag and walked away.

At the fair that evening, children carried bright lanterns. Red, blue, yellow, and green lights glowed everywhere.

Nila held the broken lantern. It looked sad.

When Tara came near, Nila turned away.

“You ruined it,” she said.

Tara’s eyes filled with tears, but she did not answer.

Later, Nila heard two younger children talking.

“Moti the goat ran inside,” one said.

“And Tara pushed the table so the goat would not eat the paper stars!” said the other.

“The lantern fell when she moved it.”

Nila became quiet.

So Tara had not been careless.

She had tried to save the lantern from becoming goat lunch.

Nila went to Tara.

“Did Moti almost eat our lantern?” she asked.

Tara nodded. “I tried to stop him. Then it fell. I was scared you would be angry.”

Nila looked at the broken lantern.

“I was angry,” she said. “But I should have listened.”

Tara whispered, “I’m sorry.”

Nila picked up some tape.

“Let’s fix it.”

Together, they taped the handle and covered the torn star with a yellow paper star.

The lantern was still bent.

But when they placed a light inside, soft stars shone on the wall.

Nila smiled.

“It still has light,” she said.
